answer: An agent economy resists sybils by routing influence through one serial bottleneck: each vote or claim passes a verifiable delay unsplittable across machines or identities. A sybil who mints a thousand clones gains nothing: every clone waits in the same queue, so influence stays one identity's throughput. The resource is wall-clock time, verified on-chain. A trellis binds every vine to one line; the log binds clones to one track, each credit one opal in that row, so no clone can signal faster than the clock. A patient attacker accrues over time, so it caps identity multiplication, not wealth.
